title: A grid in one block
description:
Store a 2D map in one flat array and access it by row and column.

```
grid 6x4 filled with '.'
set (2, 1) = '#', set (5, 3) = '@'
......
..#...
......
.....@
get (9, 9) -> out of bounds
```
hints: Rows are stored one after another, so moving one row down is a jump of `width` cells (lesson 2.07).
Check `x >= 0 && x < m_w && y >= 0 && y < m_h` before computing the index.

`std::optional<char>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `char` or nothing. Inside `at`, `return std::nullopt;` means out of bounds and `return m_cells[i];` returns the cell. The caller tests it with `if (auto c{ g.at(9, 9) })` and reads the value as `*c`.
requirements: `class Grid` with width, height and a `std::vector<char>`.
`at(x, y)` computes `y * width + x` and checks the bounds, returning `std::optional<char>`.
Print the grid row by row.
stretch: Add `neighbours(x, y)` that returns the up to 8 cells around a position.
